findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses group resource name as group id but resources are named by id only in V2
findings.body: In V2 the group-type resource is looked up by type and the callback adds groupResource.getId() (a resource UUID) to the granted set, while callers use the set as group IDs for the user search filter. Resource IDs are internal store IDs, not group IDs, so the returned set does not match group IDs and the group-membership based user filtering in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource silently returns wrong results. Resource name (group id) should be used instead.

findings.title: hasPermission looks up group resource by name but uses null-group fallback wrongly for canView/canManage without group
findings.body: hasPermission(null, ...) falls back to the all-groups resource and checks policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with a resource that may be null if the Groups type resource does not exist, causing a NullPointerException rather than a denial when the resource type resource is missing.

findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides throw UnsupportedOperationException for methods still reachable from V2 code paths
findings.body: isPermissionsEnabled and setPermissionsEnabled throw in V2, but GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled call AdminPermissions.management(...).groups().isPermissionsEnabled() and setPermissionsEnabled() on V2 when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled, so these REST endpoints now throw 500 instead of returning a meaningful response.

findings.title: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now fall back to group-based management without restoring the removed MANAGE check
findings.body: canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership in V2 now grant access via canManageByGroup (MANAGE_MEMBERS on a group), which broadens the permission model beyond what the schema documents for MAP_ROLES/MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP; this is an unintended authorization expansion relative to the stated scopes and is not covered by tests for the negative case.

findings.title: canManage() replaced default check with hasOneAdminRole, dropping V2 permission-based fallback semantics
findings.body: GroupPermissions.canManage() now only checks MANAGE_USERS role, while the removed canManageDefault delegated to the users permission evaluator. Callers relying on canManage() for the realm-level grant no longer get consistent behaviour with UserPermissions.canManage(), which uses the same role check but the base class is also used for V1 where permission-based realm-level manage was previously evaluated via users().

findings.title: Javadoc for canManage/canView/canManageGroupMembership mentions group-chain permissions the implementation does not check for every method
findings.body: The javadoc for canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership claims MANAGE_MEMBERS of the group chain grants access, and canImpersonate docs are inconsistent with code; docs and behaviour diverge, misleading integrators.

findings.title: Group removal listener is now only registered under the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check at registration time
findings.body: registerListener now checks the feature flag once when registering and no longer per event; if the feature flag state changes at runtime or differs between registration and dispatch, behaviour changes. More importantly the listener is now skipped entirely when the flag is off, which is the intended behaviour, but the change is unrelated to the PR's stated scope and untested.

findings.title: Test class has stray double semicolon and no negative test for group membership view via users endpoint
findings.body: The field declaration ends with ';;' and the view-members test only checks positive visibility; there is no test asserting that a user outside the group stays hidden when only VIEW on Groups is granted, which is the core security property of the new Groups resource type.
